t: There is no single canonical text: tales of Indian and Persian origin were joined by Arabic stories of Abbasid Baghdad and Mamluk Cairo, and the Egyptian collections kept growing into the 18th and 19th centuries.
Aladdin and Ali Baba, its best-known tales in the West, are in none of the original Arabic manuscripts; Antoine Galland added them after hearing them from Hanna Diyab in Paris in 1709.
Galland's French version of 1704 made it famous across Europe, and its frame story, nested tales and cliffhangers have since shaped writers from Voltaire to Borges and films from Méliès to Disney.
dyk: Since 1982 the International Astronomical Union has named features on Saturn's moon Enceladus after characters and places in Richard Francis Burton's translation of the Nights.
ev: Persian tales are probably translated into Arabic as Alf Layla, “The Thousand Nights”, the core of the later collection
A few lines titled The Book of the Tale of a Thousand Nights are written, the earliest known surviving fragment of the Nights
Ibn al-Nadim describes the Persian Hezār Afsān and its frame story in his Fihrist, compiled in Baghdad
A document from Cairo mentions a Jewish bookseller lending a copy of The Thousand and One Nights, the first use of the full title
The Galland Manuscript, the earliest extensive manuscript of the Nights, is written in the Syrian tradition
Antoine Galland's French translation, the first European version, begins to appear
The Bulaq edition, printed by the Egyptian government, is the first Arabic edition printed in an Arab country
Muhsin Mahdi publishes the Leiden edition, the only critical edition of the Nights to date

f.made: Many authors, translators and scholars across West Asia, Central Asia, South Asia and North Africa over many centuries; the frame story comes from the Pahlavi Persian Hezār Afsān, and the French translator Antoine Galland added tales he heard from the Syrian writer Hanna Diyab
f.form: Mostly Arabic prose, with verse for songs, riddles and heightened emotion; tales framed within tales and divided into nights, from a few hundred in some editions to 1001 or more in others
f.where: Some 114 Arabic manuscripts are known (Ibrahim Akel, 2016), only 15 of them complete; the Galland Manuscript, the earliest extensive one, is in the Bibliothèque nationale de France in Paris
f.known: Scheherazade and Shahryar; Sinbad the Sailor; Aladdin and Ali Baba, added by Galland; The Three Apples; The City of Brass and The Ebony Horse; genies, ghouls and magic lamps; stories within stories
